title: MkKill and MkExit end one task only: sibling threads of a killed capsule keep running with its capabilities and its parent cannot kill them
preconditions: Hostile capsule that spawned at least one thread (IPC bit)
Killer is the parent or a Process Manager
description: sys_kill calls teardown once for the target pid and teardown acts on that pid only; there is no group kill. A thread's parent is its spawner, so the capsule's own parent fails the is_parent check on the worker thread; when the leader finalises, children including threads are reparented to pid 1. Devices are released only when the last of the group ends. The Process Manager lists thread PCBs as rows named 'thread' and can end them one at a time, but a surviving thread can spawn new threads.
impact: Ending a capsule can leave it running with its group's capabilities and devices. Containment and availability, not escalation: no authority beyond the group's bits.
scenario: Hostile capsule spawns a worker thread.
Parent or user ends the capsule; only the leader is torn down.
The worker keeps running and can respawn threads faster than rows are killed (race not run).

steps: Traced in the source and confirmed by an independent code reading.

Reproduced on a booted kernel: a leader thread spawned a child thread, which in turn spawned a grandchild. The leader's kill of its direct child succeeded; the grandchild kept running (observed heartbeats) and was not reachable by the leader's kill (EPERM), since its parent is the thread that spawned it, not the leader. After the leader itself exited (MkExit), the grandchild was still running and producing heartbeats.
Whether a process-manager pass that ends every listed thread row individually can still end the group was not tested. A respawn race (new threads spawned faster than rows are ended) was not shown.

remediation: Make teardown and kill act on the whole thread group (or have MkKill of a leader end every member), and make the parent relation apply to group members.
